title: Can any simple change to the learning rule make lifetime learning pay in an evolving population?
question: P and R found that agents learning during their lifetime eat less than agents with fixed, evolved wiring (scalar critic -31%, per-state critic about -15%). Starting from the per-state critic, do two further changes close the gap: crediting only the executed action, or a four-times lower learning rate?
background: R: food per agent-tick 0.035 scalar, 0.042 state, 0.050 no learning (viscous, 8000 ticks). credit_chosen_only cut about half of the learned signalling rise in I. lr=0.2 is a quarter of the default 0.8. No pilot was run for this study; directions come from R and I only. Survival is not tested because no viscous population went extinct within 8000 ticks in P or R. Seeds 1700-1707 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Replication of R: a per-state critic forages better than the scalar critic
Crediting only the executed action improves foraging over the per-state critic alone
A lower learning rate improves foraging over the per-state critic alone
Learning still costs foraging with state critic plus chosen-only credit
Learning still costs foraging with state critic plus a low learning rate
